new.n: Two jars of gold coins on adjoining farms, Town of Eden (c.1920 and 1928)
new.pl: Riley and Lloyd farms side by side in the S part of sec. 32 T14N R18E, Town of Eden (1893 plat)
new.v: $1,600 in gold (1928) and $2,000 in gold (earlier), some coins dated 1850
new.st: In July 1928 W. J. 'Billy' Reilly, treasurer of the Town of Eden, was razing part of his dwelling when, the Campbellsport News reported, he found a jar in the walls holding $1,600 in gold coins, some dated 1850. 'Several years ago a Mr. Lloyd, who resided on an adjoining farm, found a jar containing $2,000 in gold coins.' The paper hedged whether it was 'Dame Fortune or our informant's imagination'. Pin is on the line between the two farms, not a spot.
new.t: Both jars were recovered. Two hoards on adjoining farms point to one old family's savings split between the places; the 1893 plat shows the Riley and Lloyd farms side by side in sec. 32, so the ground between the two farmsteads and the old fence line is the only open question. Private farms: ask permission.
src: "A Hidden Treasure?", West Bend News, 18 Jul 1928, p. 2, from the Campbellsport News (Newspapers.com 1035752359)
Plat Book of Fond du Lac County (C. M. Foote, 1893), Eden T14N R18E
US census 1930, Town of Eden: William Reilly household
pinev: 1893 Foote plat of Eden T14N R18E: 'Jas. Riley 80' in the S part of sec. 32 adjoining 'Mrs. Lloyd 120' on its W side, cemetery at Lloyd's SW corner, School No. 3 on the S line; pin on the common line of the two tracts (sec. 32 checked on BLM PLSS). The 1928 owner W. J. Reilly is not yet proven on this tract; a 1910-30 plat would settle it.
new.tovw: Lead grade F (treasure thread): both jars found
